beats: In 1932, Australia sent soldiers with machine guns to fight a flock of birds!
Twenty thousand emus had stormed the wheat farms of Western Australia.
The army sent Major Meredith, two soldiers, two Lewis guns, and ten thousand bullets.
At their first big ambush, by a dam, a gun jammed after about a dozen birds!
The rest split into small groups and ran in every direction.
An ornithologist later wrote that the emus had switched to guerrilla tactics!
So the soldiers mounted a gun on a truck and gave chase.
But the ground was so rough the gunner couldn't aim, and the emus outran the truck!
After less than a week, the army pulled out.
In Parliament, one member joked that the medals should go to the emus.
Meredith went back, and by December he claimed 986 kills.
That's ten bullets for every bird.
He said the emus could face machine guns with the invulnerability of tanks!
Two years later, farmers filed over fifty-seven thousand emu bounty claims in just six months.
Today, the emu stands on Australia's coat of arms.
The army lost the war, but the emu got the coat of arms!
